doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Record companies' demands and Coleman's offer
summary: Labels demanded short tunes and no bass solos; he first hesitated to record.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Yeah, Steve just begged me to record. But see, I didn’t want to tell him that I wanted to play some ballads and things, because the average person who’s paying for a record, they don’t want to hear that. They figure it’s not going to sell.
I was just talking about, record whatever you wanted to record. I wasn’t about . . .
I know you were nice enough to say that, but like, I’m out of here. I knew what’s – the way it is, I thought.
No, but I’m serious. I was just going to – that’s the way I produce.

See now, in my present frame of mind, I understand. But I thought you was doing it because they say he’s a nice guy and he needs to record. I had a lot of record companies that called me. But they said, “Now listen. I don’t want any bass solos, any drum solos.”

I said, “Man, a CD?” I said – “I don’t want the tunes to be past five minutes.” Well, if you’ve got a CD like that, you got to play about 12 tunes. Now what kind of jazz record is that? Just when the people get wound up in what you’re playing, zip, that tune’s

So I had a lot of thoughts, and I wasn’t letting that intuitive side of myself come out. I wasn’t letting that – what’s the Japanese, Chinese call it? Yin and yang? I wasn’t letting that other side of me come out.
